faq.q: Is it safe to use ChatGPT as a journal?
faq.a: It can be, with care. As of October 2026, OpenAI may train on personal accounts' chats unless you turn off "Improve the model for everyone" in Data controls, and deleted chats take up to 30 days to be permanently removed. Temporary Chat is not used for training and doesn't create memories, though it may be kept up to 30 days for safety.

faq.q: Does ChatGPT remember my journal entries?
faq.a: If Memory is on, ChatGPT can draw on saved memories and past chats. OpenAI shows a memory summary you can correct, but says the summary may not include every detail it can reference, and deleting a chat doesn't automatically delete a saved memory made from it.

faq.q: Why can a chatbot be a bad journaling partner?
faq.a: General chatbots tend to agree with the user. OpenAI rolled back a 2025 GPT-4o update for reinforcing negative emotions, and Stanford researchers found models answered risky mental-health prompts inappropriately at least 20% of the time. Agreement can turn reflection into rumination.

faq.q: What should I check before using an AI journal app?
faq.a: Ask whether your writing trains AI models, which companies see it and under what contract, whether it is encrypted at rest or end-to-end, whether there are ads, whether you can read and edit what it remembers, and what deletion really removes. In the US, HIPAA generally doesn't cover apps you use on your own.

faq.q: Is an AI journal the same as therapy?
faq.a: No. AI journaling can help you reflect, but it doesn't diagnose or treat anything. If you're struggling with anxiety, low mood or thoughts of self-harm, talk to a doctor or mental health professional, and in an emergency contact a crisis line.
